description.value: A cross-sectional fMRI study examined the development of cognitive reappraisal and emotion regulation in older children, adolescents and young adults.

spans.text: the present study used a cross-sectional design to examine the development of emotion regulation in older children, adolescents and young adults

Thirty-eight participants between the ages of 10 and 22 completed the experimental procedure and were compensated for their time.

value: Emotional reactivity was associated with significantly greater activation for negative than neutral pictures in the look condition, including the insula, visual cortex and several subcortical regions, including the amygdala.
There were no age-related differences in emotional reactivity measured by self-reported affect or amygdala activation.

spans.text: Consistent with prior work in adults, with all participants included, we observed strong significant activations related to emotional reactivity (look negative > look neutral contrast) in the insula, visual cortex and several subcortical regions (including the amygdala).
Peaks are identified with Talairach coordinates.
